description: Still dealing with mechanical issues in the design of the controller.

banner.text: Locate and correct the source of the mechanical errors in the controller design.

body: After a few times of struggling to fasten the two halves of the controller body together, from buttons being misaligned on the front and/or the PCB on the back... I added cantilever clips to the PCB. Now assembling the controller is much easier. Also added some stylization to the directional pad... Just in case someone needs visual clues to what each button does... I'm quickly running out of issues with the printing and shell/button designs. I fear I'll soon have to go back to the PCB to fix my mistakes there😮‍💨😮‍💨... For those who have not seen the PCB, there it is. I never posted about it, but eagle eyes could have spotted that it was there in some pictures I posted of the shells fastened. These are the first 5 boards. I'll rework them and have another set made... If those work they will take on a more contoured shape of the shell and silkscreen printing to aid in assembly.
I added some cantelever clips to hold the PCB in place while assembling the controller.
The PCB is designed so that the shoulder buttons are on a break-away from the main board.
Here is a new board next to an assembled PCB.
Added direction indicators to the DPad in case anyone doesnt know which direction each button traverses you.
